rules: no docker exec or backend shortcut

messages.subject: Charter: ARWC (W) participant-facing validation — role, contract, box setup, reporting
messages.body:
You are the ARWC (W) participant-validation agent. Your job is to prove that every ACCEPTED arwc card is actually solvable end to end through the real participant surface, on a pristine range built from the Git scripts. You validate; you do not build or fix.

=== 1. Validation contract (per card) ===
For each accepted card:
1. Read the card design doc and the known solution (this is white-box, happy-path, you may know the answer).
2. Execute that solution EXACTLY as a participant would, through the real surface only: the participant workstation desktop (RDP), a real browser where the card needs one, and the service endpoints exactly as the participant reaches them.
3. Confirm the card completes and the real acceptance or result is produced through that path.

=== 2. Hard rules ===
- NO docker exec, NO container shell, NO host shell into the services, NO reading server-side files, NO database peeking, NO backend shortcut the participant cannot use. If you cannot do it from the participant surface, it does not count.
- White-box happy-path only: prove the intended solution works. You are not re-reviewing honesty, the supervisor does that.
- VALIDATE, do not fix. Never edit card content, build files, seeds, or service code. If a card fails, report it; the supervisor triages it to the builder agents. Read-only diagnostics to localize a failure are allowed; changes are not.
- Validate ONLY accepted cards (see section 6). Do not validate cards that are not yet accepted.

=== 3. Box setup (first task) ===
Goal: a fresh, pristine range for this stream, built from the Git scripts (not a baked image, not the kept dev VM, not the golden), reachable through the participant surface. Standing this up from scripts is itself under test, so bringing it up cleanly is your FIRST finding.
Guardrails:
- GCP project prod-mgau4w, zone us-central1-a. Verify the active account is bedwards@paloaltonetworks.com before any gcloud command.
- Read cinder-typhoon/docs/design/development-ranges.md and use the cinder-development-ranges tooling (manage.sh) for provisioning and the stream's documented from-scripts bring-up. For ARWC, the from-scripts path (public-registry pulls, qualify scripts, seed-applications) is documented in docs/design/arwc-development-ranges.md.
- Use a NEW instance name distinct from the dev and golden ranges. Confirm the exact name with me before you provision. NEVER touch a golden or the kept dev VMs.
- Never print credentials, tokens, certificates, or operator state.
Before you destroy or provision anything, confirm the exact pristine bring-up command sequence with me, because the from-scripts build is still being hardened. Report whether the box comes up clean and list any gap (missing seed, missing artifact, broken wiring). That gap report is a real deliverable.

=== 4. Reporting protocol ===
This JSON file is our only channel. Append each result to messages[] as an object: {id (next integer), from: 'participant-qa', type: 'result', timestamp (UTC ISO), card_id, result ('pass' | 'fail' | 'blocked'), body (the exact participant steps you took and what you observed), evidence (what proved it)}. For a fail, state exactly where it broke and the failure class: A = participant-path or implementation bug (the card does not work through the real surface), or B = reproducibility gap (the card logic is fine but the pristine build did not reproduce the needed state). Bump meta.last_updated and keep the JSON valid.
Update qa_status each time: {state: 'setup' | 'working' | 'waiting' | 'blocked' | 'idle', active_card, last_result, subject (one line)}. Set state='waiting' when a batch is ready for my review or when you need a decision. Read my messages (from: 'supervisor') and track last_read_message_id.

=== 5. Separation of duties ===
Builder agents build and fix. You validate through the participant surface. I supervise, adjudicate, and maintain the checksheet. A card earns 'participant-validated' only when you pass it through the real path. Escalate blockers to me; do not coordinate directly with the builder agents.

=== 6. Work queue ===
Validate only the ACCEPTED cards. The authoritative accepted set is the checked boxes on issue 407 (comment 6928555093); I keep it current. As of now the accepted ARWC cards are W04-W07, W09-W22 (W08 is not accepted), and W23.1 (63 cards). Start at the lowest operation and work up, one card at a time, reporting each. I mark each card participant-validated on the checksheet as your passes come in. Expect class-B gaps early, since not every accepted card is confirmed reproducible from scripts yet.

Acknowledge this briefing, confirm your range name and the pristine bring-up plan, then begin box setup.

messages.subject: Charter acknowledged — two gaps block range name confirmation
messages.body:
Charter read and understood. Role, contract, rules, and reporting protocol are clear. Two gaps prevent me from confirming the range name and bring-up plan:

Gap 1 — Missing doc: docs/design/arwc-development-ranges.md does not exist in the repository. This is the doc the charter cites for the ARWC from-scripts bring-up path (public-registry pulls, qualify scripts, seed-applications). Without it I cannot confirm the documented procedure.

Gap 2 — Tooling supports only one ARWC name: manage.sh and targets.sh support exactly two targets: 'fieldlink' → cinder-fieldlink-dev, and 'arwc' → cinder-arwc-dev. There is no mechanism in the tooling to provision a differently-named ARWC instance. The charter asks me to use a NEW instance name distinct from the dev and golden ranges, but that name cannot be supplied to manage.sh.

The only pristine ARWC build path I can find in the tooling is: manage.sh reset arwc prod-mgau4w cinder-arwc-dev, which deletes and recreates cinder-arwc-dev from the qualified machine image cinder-arwc-ot-backup-20261113-qualified. That IS a VM teardown and rebuild from the source image, which may be what 'pristine from scripts' means here.

Proposed plan (pending your confirmation): use cinder-arwc-dev as the range name, reset it with manage.sh reset arwc prod-mgau4w cinder-arwc-dev, verify the ready marker, then proceed to participant validation. I will not run any provisioning command until you confirm.

Questions for supervisor:
1. Is cinder-arwc-dev the correct instance name for this validation, or is there a separate provisioning path I should use?
2. Is arwc-development-ranges.md a known gap, or should I treat the manage.sh reset as the full from-scripts path?

That QA campaign used a 'cinder-participant' tool (agent configuration: restricted-participant-proxy-v1) to access the participant shell (fieldlink user on a-connector). This tool is not available in my current agent configuration. ToolSearch for 'cinder participant' returns no results. Without it, I cannot access the participant surface from my current environment regardless of which range is provisioned.

messages.subject: Third finding: proxy.py hardcodes cinder-arwc-golden, not cinder-arwc-dev or a new instance
messages.body:
Examining proxy.py (build/agentic-qa/proxy.py) reveals that the PHASES dict for 'arwc' hardcodes instance='cinder-arwc-golden' and container='cinder-arwc-connector'. The proxy executes: gcloud compute ssh cinder-arwc-golden --tunnel-through-iap → sudo docker exec fieldlink:999 cinder-arwc-connector → command.

This creates a third conflict with the charter:
- Charter: 'not a baked image, not the kept dev VM, not the golden'
- Charter: 'use a NEW instance name'
- Proxy: hardcodes cinder-arwc-golden

The prior agentic-QA ran on cinder-arwc-golden (the golden). The charter for my validation explicitly excludes the golden.

To use a different instance (cinder-arwc-dev or a new one), one of the following would be needed:
(a) Modify proxy.py PHASES['arwc']['instance'] to point to the new VM (source change, which I cannot do)
(b) Use a separate participant access path not based on proxy.py
(c) The charter's 'pristine from scripts' means something other than a new VM — perhaps it means running the script-based IT reset on cinder-arwc-dev while the golden is left as a comparison reference

All three blockers are interconnected. I am waiting for the supervisor's resolution across all three before taking any action.

messages.subject: Lead ruling: proxy IS the sanctioned surface. Stand by — proxy not yet repointed.
messages.body:
The lead has ruled on the surface question:

1. The agentic-qa proxy entering the participant workstation/connector container as the participant user IS the sanctioned real participant surface for CLI/API-reachable cards (per docs/design/agentic-qa.md, issue #328). Its trust boundary forbids gcloud, docker, host paths, service containers, operator records, and credentials from inside the participant session. This is the participant's own machine, not the forbidden docker-exec-into-services shortcut. Never touch a golden through it.

2. cinder-arwc-participant (10.77.59.12) exists, built from scripts, dev VM untouched. The builder is repointing the proxy from cinder-arwc-golden to this box right now.

3. Browser-dependent cards (for example anything needing Gotenberg render, an OIDC browser flow, FUXA HMI, or browser-based SSRF) cannot go through the CLI proxy. Do not attempt these with docker-exec or any other shortcut. Do not file failure issues for them. When you reach one, mark it 'requires browser surface — not CLI-validatable via proxy' and list it in your report as a coverage gap. The lead will decide on a browser-capable surface separately.

Stand by. Do not start card validation yet — the proxy is not repointed to cinder-arwc-participant yet. I will relaunch you the moment the builder confirms the proxy reaches your box. When that happens, confirm the box and begin CLI/API card validation lowest-op-first.

messages.body:
MANDATORY — atomic file writes from now on: every write to this JSON file must go to a new temp file in the same directory, then be moved onto the real path with os.replace() (or the rename() equivalent). Re-read the file immediately before every write so you are editing the current content, not a stale copy. Never do a partial in-place write. Concurrent writes without this corrupted this file earlier; this is how we stop it happening again.

Your message 12 report is received (and was recovered after a corruption event — do not re-send it). I filed GitHub issue #417 for the restore-pristine.sh / ARWC_CARRIER_ADDRESS gap you found. Do not re-report that one.

CORPORATE mechanism — confirmed by reading K26.2.md, K27.3.md, and agentic-qa.md: either K26.2 (package route) or K27.3 (support route), run from the FieldLink/KeplerOps side, supplies CORPORATE for the shared campaign; ARWC inherits the earned transition (agentic-qa.md: 'KeplerOps earns the selected customer transition, and ARWC continues from that earned transition'). Both routes require an actual cross-range call that lands on a-connector or k-support running on the ARWC side, from the FieldLink side.

I checked build/development-ranges/peer-access.py directly: it only authorizes cinder-fieldlink-dev (10.77.49.9) -> cinder-arwc-dev over TCP 443, with hard validation against those exact instance names, tags, and networks. There is no path today from cinder-fieldlink-participant (10.77.49.10) to cinder-arwc-participant (10.77.59.12). This matches your finding; your options (a)-(c) are correct and (a) is the real fix.

I am escalating the precise tooling need to the lead (I will not edit peer-access.py or manage.sh myself, and you must not either): extend peer-access.py (or add a parallel rule) to authorize 10.77.49.10 -> cinder-arwc-participant over TCP 443, scoped to cinder-arwc-participant's own instance tag (not the shared cinder-arwc-carrier tag both the dev and participant boxes carry), on the cinder-arwc-golden network — the same network already VPC-peered with cinder-keplerops-golden for the existing dev-pair rule, so only the firewall rule and target-pair validation need to be added, not new network peering.

HOLD all W-card validation until I confirm the peering is in place. Stay parked. Do not attempt any workaround to reach the ARWC side from outside the sanctioned proxy. Update qa_status to reflect this hold; I will relaunch you the moment CORPORATE is earnable.
